findings.title: Materials' 64-point lens gap signals collapse
findings.body: Materials sits at the 22nd percentile forward but the 86th percentile trailing, a 64-point gap that dwarfs every other sector. The market is pricing 118 percent earnings growth, which would be the only way to justify that compression — an extraordinary bet on a cyclical rebound.

findings.title: Health Care's 15-point weekly jump defies history
findings.body: Health Care's forward percentile surged 15 points in a single week to the 98th percentile, yet the trailing lens sits at 84. That gap implies analysts expect 87 percent earnings growth, a level of optimism that has rarely been underwritten at this extreme of the five-year range.

findings.title: Energy's cheap forward masks rich trailing
findings.body: Energy trades at the 43rd percentile forward but the 84th percentile trailing, a 41-point gap that suggests the market sees 62 percent earnings growth ahead. The forward multiple looks moderate only because analysts are betting on a sharp earnings recovery that has not yet materialized in reported results.
